newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian Q1 retail sales up, but job numbers fall.
newsitem.headline: Colombian Q1 retail sales up, but job numbers fall.

text.p: Retail sales in Colombia, excluding fuel, rose 1.90 percent in the first quarter of the year compared with the same period a year ago, boosted by a solid 3.94 percent rise in March, the National Planning Department (DANE) said.
It said employment in the retail sector fell by 6.85 percent during the same time period, however, adding to the steady increase in joblessness seen since the beginning of 1995.

Retail sales, excluding gasoline and other fuel, slumped by 2.94 percent in the first quarter of 1996. As a result, this year's comparative growth -- despite a 1.22 percent contraction in first quarter gross domestic product -- is likely to be dismissed by most economic analysts as insignificant.
Rising unemployment in the retail sector is important, however, since any future growth in sales is unlikely to come against the backdrop of growing joblessness.
Colombia's overall urban unemployment rate was running at 12.7 percent in the first quarter of the year -- the highest level in nine years -- and up from 11.3 percent at the end of 1996.
